articles.title: ‘Massive difference between words and actions’: Ex-India cricketer’s blunt take on Ravindra Jadeja’s snub
articles.summary: Former India opener Aakash Chopra has questioned the selectors’ decision to leave Ravindra Jadeja out of the entire five-match ODI series against New
articles.body: Former India opener Aakash Chopra has questioned the selectors’ decision to leave Ravindra Jadeja out of the entire five-match ODI series against New Zealand, pointing to what he sees as a contradiction between the team management’s stated plans and its selection choices.India are scheduled to play five ODIs against New Zealand, beginning in Auckland on November 4. Axar Patel has been preferred over Jadeja as the left-arm spin-bowling all-rounder, despite the Indian think tank previously indicating that Jadeja remains part of its plans for the 2027 World Cup.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Chopra said Jadeja’s absence had not received enough attention and questioned the credibility of the assurances given about the veteran’s future in the team."Ravindra Jadeja not being there is a big thing. Many people haven't spoken about it. You are playing him very little anyway. You said that he is an integral part of our team, that he is part of your 2027 World Cup plans, but it doesn't seem like that, because there is a massive difference being seen in what you say and what you do," he said.Chopra pointed out that Jadeja had featured against the West Indies but was not played in the third match of that series either. The all-rounder has now been left out of both the first three and the final two matches against New Zealand.The former India opener believes Axar may have moved well ahead of Jadeja in the race for a place in the squad for the 2027 World Cup, suggesting the selectors might already have settled on their preferred option."You played him against the West Indies just now, and you didn't play him the third match there either. Here, you have neither picked him for the first three matches nor the last two matches. Axar Patel has run so far ahead in this race that it seems like the selectors have made up their minds about Ravindra Jadeja," he observed.While acknowledging that Jadeja's white-ball numbers have declined, Chopra said the selection pattern appeared to indicate that India were gradually moving away from the experienced all-rounder. He, however, stopped short of declaring whether that was the right decision.Chopra questions Manav Suthar’s omission from Test squadJadeja was not the only selection decision that drew Chopra's attention. The former cricketer also questioned why left-arm spinner Manav Suthar had not been included in India's squad for the two-Test series against New Zealand.Chopra highlighted Suthar's impressive start to his international career, pointing out that the spinner had taken 23 wickets in his first three matches. He also recalled that Suthar was named Player of the Match in his debut game and had been India's leading bowler during the tour of Sri Lanka."Manav Suthar's name is not there. Let that sink in. He has a three-match career in total, in which he was the Player of the Match in the first match. He was the pick of the Indian bowlers in Sri Lanka," he said.Chopra acknowledged that Jadeja remained ahead of Suthar in the pecking order, but wondered whether the younger spinner could have been considered instead of Washington Sundar."I know only one of Jadeja or Manav Suthar can play, and Jadeja is ahead in that race, but you cannot ignore Manav Suthar's 23 wickets in three matches. Could his name have been there in place of Washington Sundar?" Chopra observed.The commentator also stressed that the selectors should speak to Suthar and explain why he had been overlooked after such a promising start. To underline the significance of his returns, Chopra compared taking 23 wickets in three Tests to scoring three hundreds in as many matches.India's ODI squads for New Zealand tourFirst three ODIs: Shubman Gill (C), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer (VC), KL Rahul (WK), Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Anshul Kamboj, Gurnoor Brar, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Ishan Kishan (WK), Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna* and Kuldeep Yadav.Fourth and fifth ODIs: Shreyas Iyer (C), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Tilak Varma, Ishan Kishan (WK, VC), Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Kumar Kushagra (WK), Mohammed Siraj, Yash Thakur and Kuldeep Yadav.India’s Test squad: Shubman Gill [C], Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul [VC], Devdutt Padikkal, Rishabh Pant [WK, availability is subject to fitness clearance], Dhruv Jurel [WK], Ravindra Jadeja, Anshul Kamboj, Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep, Sai Sudharsan, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar, Kuldeep Yadav, Mohammed Siraj.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Armed with MS Dhoni’s advice, Kartik Sharma set for captaincy debut
articles.summary: Jaipur: When Kartik Sharma, a young wicketkeeper-batter from Bharatpur district, marked his guard on his red-ball debut two seasons ago, he announced his
articles.body: Jaipur: When Kartik Sharma, a young wicketkeeper-batter from Bharatpur district, marked his guard on his red-ball debut two seasons ago, he announced his arrival with authority. He slammed a blistering 115 off 113 balls against Uttarakhand in the Ranji Trophy 2024-25. That initial breakthrough set the tone for a domestic journey built on an unwavering appetite for runs.He truly became elemental to the chatter last year when his explosive six-hitting ability during pre-season trials caught the eye of various IPL franchises, culminating in a Rs14.20 crore contract with the Chennai Super Kings (CSK). Now, at just 20 years of age, he finds himself thrust with the bigger responsibility of leading the senior Rajasthan side. Following left-arm spinner Manav Suthar's departure to New Zealand for India ‘A’ duty, the young 'keeper-batter steps up to lead a side riding high on confidence, having secured three points via a crucial first-innings lead in their opener against Tamil Nadu in Group ‘D’ fixture.Speaking on the eve of the clash against Railways, Kartik opened up about taking over the captaincy reins and said, "I have captained Rajasthan during Under-19 days. I will try to make the team as comfortable as I can. There are a few seniors while most of them are my contemporaries in the side, so I will ensure I remain as humble with them as possible."Kartik’s gritty knock of 42 off 75 balls in the second innings against Tamil Nadu showcased a new dimension to his batting. He credits his high-stakes stint under CSK umbrella for sharpening his match awareness and instilling the patience required to play according to the situationA definitive piece of advice from franchise veteran MS Dhoni has shifted his approach away from brute force toward timing and technical precision. "When I went to Chennai I was a little injured and that is why my batting wasn't going very well. Bhaiya told me to focus on timing. He said that you aren't someone who hits power shots, whatever your timing is, that is your power, so play according to that,” he shared.Kartik has seamlessly integrated this sense of responsibility into his batting, balancing his natural boundary-clearing instincts with a refined technique. “Six-hitting is definitely there, but I am also working on grounded shots and doing my practice for that," he added.Addressing the composition of a dressing room that is decidedly youthful, Kartik sees the clean slate as a strength rather than a setback. "Nothing negative, just the positive is that all are young boys, young blood, so everyone plays together," Kartik stated.Rajasthan enter the fixture holding a distinct psychological edge from their previous outing, while Railways arrive looking to bounce back hard after conceding a first-innings lead to Uttarakhand.For Kartik and his youthful troops, the overarching objective remains focused on the ultimate prize. "The target is to win as many matches as possible," Kartik concluded.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘We've matched the defending champions’: West Indies head coach Daren Sammy after 2-2 India T20I draw
articles.summary: West Indies head coach Daren Sammy believes his team has taken a major step forward after drawing the five-match T20I series 2-2 against India.
articles.body: West Indies head coach Daren Sammy believes his team has taken a major step forward after drawing the five-match T20I series 2-2 against India. The final match in Bengaluru was abandoned due to rain, but Sammy said the team's performances showed that the players are regaining confidence and can compete with the world's best sides.Sammy also highlighted the need for greater financial support to help West Indies cricket grow and maintain its place in international cricket.Sammy sees confidence returning to West IndiesSammy said West Indies had entered the series with many people doubting their chances against India. However, the players proved they could challenge the reigning T20 world champions on their home ground."It's a true reflection of how all the teams have played, especially for our guys. I'm pretty sure when the series started, we probably didn't have a chance. But that was just the opinion of others. We would want to win because of something we've not done forever in India, so it would have been nice. I think the cup still is in our favour because we won the home leg the last time we played (in 2023) 3-2,” Sammy told reporters in the post-match press conference.He added that the team's ability to match India and outperform them in certain areas showed how much progress the players had made.“We understand what success means to us; we don't ever take for granted where we are as a team and the challenges that we face. We just look to make those strides, and I think after this series we've taken a massive step. We played against the defending champions, and we've matched them (and) in certain areas we've outplayed them, especially in their backyard,” he added.Sammy calls for financial supportBeyond the team's results, Sammy stressed that West Indies cricket needs financial backing to secure its future. He pointed to the sport's rich history in the Caribbean and its contribution to fans and businesses around the world.He said the team's recent performances could help attract the support needed to strengthen the regional game.“I think it's important; my mom always says you must have a care factor. No matter what you do in life, the human nature should never lose that care factor. I think we're in a position where we need somebody to put a (hand around the shoulder) of the West Indies cricket. Financially, that is, and series like this, here in India, against the best team in the world, puts us in a conversation closer to that,” he said.Sammy also welcomed the renewed confidence and fighting spirit among his players.“All the guys in the dressing room, they've gone out there and played with intent and I think what was good to see is that the swagger is back, the confidence is back. It started during the World Cup and you could see guys enjoying, and there was a willingness to win. That's where it starts; the belief that we belong where we are, and to have the performances that says you belong there. Hopefully, right now it's just been consistent,” he added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘No option but to bat at 5 or 6’: Tilak Varma on adapting to new role in India’s T20I setup
articles.summary: India vice-captain Tilak Varma has acknowledged that moving away from his preferred No.
articles.body: India vice-captain Tilak Varma has acknowledged that moving away from his preferred No. 3 position to bat lower down the order presents a challenge, but the 23-year-old is confident that regular practice and mental preparation will help him adjust to the demands of his new role.Tilak has increasingly been used at No. 5 and 6 in T20Is as India continue to settle on their batting combination. While the Hyderabad batter admits that he finds it easier to bat higher up the order, he is focused on becoming a reliable finisher for the team.Speaking after the fifth and final T20I against the West Indies was washed out on Saturday night, Tilak said adapting to different batting positions requires considerable work, particularly when the responsibility is to close out games."It's not that easy to change the numbers from 3 to 5 and 6. It will be slightly challenging. But I have been working on that. How can I finish the games? I have said that I love finishing the games for the country," he said."So, for me as an individual, if you see, it will be easier batting at 3. But unfortunately, now I should bat at 5 or 6 because we have got that combination at the top right now."The left-hander's record at No. 6 offers encouragement. Across nine matches in that position, he averages 65.66 at a strike rate of 195. In 26 combined innings at Nos. 5 and 6, he has scored at an average of 46 and a strike rate of 158.However, the arrival of Ishan Kishan, captain Shreyas Iyer's presence at No. 4 and the management's decision to continue with the Abhishek Sharma-Sanju Samson opening combination have left Tilak with a reduced role in the middle order.Kishan has been batting at No. 3 and has impressed in the position, leaving Tilak with little choice but to embrace the finishing responsibilities."Kishan is batting at number 3 now, and he is batting really brilliantly there. So, for me now, I think there is no option but to bat at 5 and 6 and do the job for the team."So, I am mentally prepared for that role. And if you see the last few games, I have won from there. So, I am pretty confident to do well there as well," he added.Tilak working on his finishing skillsTilak said he has been putting in extra work in the nets to expand his shot-making range and improve his ability to score quickly when batting with limited time at the crease.He explained that players operating at Nos. 5 and 6 often have only five or six overs to make an impact, making it important to capitalise on scoring opportunities, including when bowlers deliver slower balls within their hitting range."Yeah, we should do that, otherwise, it will be slightly tough. When you go in to bat as a finisher, if a slower one comes into your arc, you should go for 6. Otherwise, if you see in T20, most of the time, if you go into that role of 5 or 6, you will get a maximum of 5 to 6 overs to bat."So, I have changed personally. I have been in this role in my childhood as well. I have got the shots going all over the ground. So, I am confident that if I bat at 3 or 5, I have got the technique to adapt. So, if I practise for 1 or 2 days, I can do any role for the team."Now, if I come back to No. 3, I can adapt after a day or two of practice. I am confident of batting anywhere," he noted.Busy schedule no excuse, says India vice-captainIndia's players have endured a packed run of fixtures over the past few months, travelling across the United Kingdom, Japan and India. The team will soon head to New Zealand for an all-format tour.Tilak admitted that the demands of consecutive series, different time zones and changing conditions can be difficult, particularly for younger players. However, he stressed that handling such challenges is part of playing international cricket."It will be slightly challenging. But as professional cricketers, we can't give any excuse because when we play back-to-back series, there will be different time zones and all those things. We are used to it now. If you see, for any youngster coming into the team, it will be slightly challenging."But again, you are playing for the country and at the highest level. So, as I said, you should be mentally strong enough to prepare for any challenge, any conditions so that you can become a bigger player," he added.Tilak highlights positives from West Indies seriesDespite the challenges, Tilak believes India have several encouraging takeaways from the West Indies series that they can carry into the upcoming assignments in New Zealand.He pointed to the team's consistent run-scoring, with India crossing the 200-run mark in every match, as a major positive. He also acknowledged the contributions of Nitish Reddy, Shivam Dube and Naman Dhir."There have been quite a few good things. Especially in the batting, every game we have scored over 200 plus. So, that's a big positive, and that too, we haven't got a proper all-rounder in the team. We have played both Nitish (Reddy) and (Shivam) Dubey as well. But both have done decently well."Then Naman (Dhir) bowled well under pressure. As an off-spinner, bowling to right-handers, and that too against a big-gun team like the West Indies."So, there are a few good points for us to take into the upcoming series. As a team, we have introspected a few things in the bowling as well. So, hopefully, we will do well in the New Zealand series," he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘RR are at the top of the list’: Ashwin makes big revelation on Hardik Pandya trade
articles.summary: Speculation surrounding Hardik Pandya's future with Mumbai Indians has intensified, with former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin weighing in on reports
articles.body: Speculation surrounding Hardik Pandya's future with Mumbai Indians has intensified, with former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin weighing in on reports linking the star all-rounder with a potential move to Chennai Super Kings ahead of the next Indian Premier League season.Rumours of a possible trade between the five-time champions have gained traction on social media, with suggestions that CSK icon MS Dhoni could personally persuade Hardik to join the Chennai franchise. However, Ashwin believes that while the all-rounder's arrival would strengthen CSK, a deal remains a distant possibility.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ashwin acknowledged the appeal of having Hardik in the CSK setup but stopped short of endorsing the speculation surrounding the proposed move."There have been conversations that Dhoni will personally convince Hardik Pandya to come to CSK. It will be a great addition for CSK. But in my opinion, it is a real far-shot," said Ashwin.The former India spinner also offered an alternative possibility, claiming that Rajasthan Royals could be better placed to secure Hardik's services if a trade materialises."From what I've heard, RR are at the top of the list in the Hardik trade," he added.Ashwin's comments come at a crucial time for Mumbai Indians, who are preparing for a significant change in their coaching setup following the departure of head coach Mahela Jayawardene.Mahela Jayawardene leaves Mumbai Indians after second stintMumbai Indians confirmed on Saturday that Jayawardene had ended his second spell as head coach after two seasons in charge.The 49-year-old Sri Lankan, who guided the franchise to three IPL titles during his first tenure, returned to the role ahead of the 2025 season after previously coaching MI between 2017 and 2022.His second stint produced mixed results. Mumbai finished fourth in the 2025 season before suffering defeat in Qualifier 2, while their 2026 campaign proved considerably more disappointing, with the five-time champions ending the tournament in ninth place.The franchise must now identify a new head coach with the November 15 IPL retention deadline less than a month away.With a major decision pending in the dugout and trade speculation surrounding Hardik continuing, Mumbai Indians face an important period ahead of the next season.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Hardik Pandya is irreplaceable': Sunil Gavaskar believes India should stop searching for a direct replacement for all-rounder
articles.summary: Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar believes India should stop searching for a direct replacement for Hardik Pandya, as the all-rounder brings a unique
articles.body: Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar believes India should stop searching for a direct replacement for Hardik Pandya, as the all-rounder brings a unique combination of batting and bowling that is difficult to match.Instead, he advised the team to consider players who can perform different roles while maintaining a strong bowling attack.Gavaskar shared his views after India's five-match T20I series against the West Indies ended in a 2-2 draw. The final match in Bengaluru was abandoned due to rain.Gavaskar wants India to strengthen its bowlingGavaskar suggested that India should play at least four specialist bowlers and use all-rounders as the fifth and sixth bowling options. He warned that selecting too many batters could weaken the bowling unit and cost India matches."We sometimes get a little bit carried away with trying to find a replacement for Hardik Pandya. Hardik Pandya is irreplaceable. If you can't find somebody of his calibre, then go with somebody who will do a slightly different job," Gavaskar said on JioStar.He pointed to Naman Dhir as an example of a player who can contribute with both bat and ball. Dhir scored an unbeaten 24 off just six balls in the rain-hit final T20I."Naman Dhir is doing that job. He's bowling his overs well, and look at the way he batted in this game," he said.Gavaskar also highlighted the importance of backing spin bowlers and helping them maintain confidence, even when they are not regular members of the playing XI."The moment you go with batting up to number eight, you weaken your bowling, and that's where you get beaten," he said.Chopra assesses Abhishek Sharma's performanceGavaskar added that the abandoned final denied India a chance to assess their bowling in the shortened match.Former India opener Aakash Chopra also reviewed Abhishek Sharma's performance, saying the left-handed batter was not at his usual best during the series. However, he stressed that inconsistent performances are normal in an aggressive batting approach."In the last game, when he didn't get much strike, he looked a bit scratchy. He didn't get any rhythm at all, and let's discount whatever happened in this game. So, he was a bit below par by his standards in the series, but that is also going to happen."Chopra added that players aiming for strike rates around 200 cannot be expected to score consistently in every match.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shubman Gill scores just one run on Ranji Trophy return ahead of New Zealand Tests
articles.summary: Shubman Gill had a disappointing return to domestic red-ball cricket, scoring just one run for Punjab against Chhattisgarh in their Ranji Trophy Elite
articles.body: Shubman Gill had a disappointing return to domestic red-ball cricket, scoring just one run for Punjab against Chhattisgarh in their Ranji Trophy Elite Group B match in New Chandigarh on Sunday.The India Test captain is using the domestic competition to prepare for the upcoming two-match Test series against New Zealand.Gill came in to bat at No. 4 after Vihaan Malhotra was dismissed on the first ball of the 26th over. However, his innings lasted only five deliveries.Chhattisgarh bowler Ajay Mandal bowled him on the third ball of the 27th over, leaving Punjab at 68/3. Gill managed just one run, which came off the second ball he faced.Gill prepares for New Zealand TestsGill was added to Punjab's squad at the last minute to get some red-ball match practice before India's Test series against New Zealand, which begins on November 19.Before joining the Test preparations, Gill is expected to play in the first three ODIs of India's five-match series against New Zealand, scheduled from November 4 to 15. His deputy, Shreyas Iyer, will take over as ODI captain after Gill leaves to prepare for the Tests.Despite his early dismissal in the Ranji Trophy, Gill has enjoyed an impressive year in international cricket. In three Tests this year, he has scored 200 runs in four innings at an average of 50.00, including one century and one half-century.Impressive international formGill has been particularly successful in limited-overs cricket. Across 15 international matches this year, he has scored 1,095 runs at an average of 91.25, with four centuries and six half-centuries in 15 innings.His highest score during this run was an unbeaten 223 against the West Indies in the second ODI. With the New Zealand Test series approaching, Gill will be looking to regain his touch in the coming matches and lead India in the crucial red-ball contest.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Consistency is overrated in T20s’: Former India cricketer explains fine line between form and failure
articles.summary: Former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara believes consistency is overrated for top-order batters in T20 cricket, backing Sanju Samson to regain form with one
articles.body: Former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara believes consistency is overrated for top-order batters in T20 cricket, backing Sanju Samson to regain form with one good innings ahead of India's upcoming multi-format tour of New Zealand."Consistency should be there, but for the top order, I think consistency is overrated in T20s," Pujara said while analysing Samson's fluctuating returns on JioHotstar's 'Out or Not Out', as quoted by news agency PTI."He is never out of form. The kind of player Sanju Samson has been in the T20 format; his form fluctuates. But it is always a matter of one innings. He plays one good innings, and he is back in form.""So, you cannot say that this player is not in form. In the T20 format, you are bound to have failures. Who doesn't get out in T20s?" he added.India recently ended their five-match T20I series against the West Indies in a 2-2 draw. They will begin their multi-format tour of New Zealand with the shortest format.Pujara also expressed doubts over whether Samson and teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi could feature together in India's playing XI in New Zealand. He said the conditions could require more all-rounders, leaving less room for specialist batters in the top order."Vaibhav playing every game seems a bit difficult in New Zealand because there you need more all-rounders, either a spin all-rounder or a seaming all-rounder. So, there you don't need a lot of batters, especially in the top order," he said."Either Sanju Samson can open or Vaibhav. I don't think both can be part of the playing XI in New Zealand conditions. So, Vaibhav will have to wait, but he will get opportunities."However, Pujara said Sooryavanshi could still get a chance if the conditions or a player's fitness opened up a spot in the team."If the spot opens up for him based on conditions or players' fitness, that's fine. But both Sanju and Vaibhav cannot be in the playing XI in New Zealand," he said.Former India assistant coach Abhishek Nayar also backed Samson, saying the wicketkeeper-batter's place in the team would come under scrutiny after a few quiet games, but one big innings could silence the questions."Sanju plays with everyone's emotions because he won't score runs for two matches, and everyone starts raising questions," Nayar said.Nayar added that Sooryavanshi might have to wait for his opportunities, with team balance and the need for a left-right batting combination likely to influence India's selection decisions.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
